openings.claim: Future capability: an obsolete hold address can still route the clerk to the correct book after household-name errors and shelf/cart moves, without rebuilding the surname order. Paper forwarding pointers could supply this capability; correct identity binding and reliable pointer creation remain unproven dependencies.
openings.delta: A storage address becomes a persistent route: when a coded hold moves, its old address retains a pointer to its new address. Divider cards merely narrow a region, and the daily exception slip can become stale. This proposal evaluates a bounded enabling probe, not achievement of the pickup target.
openings.prediction: After two recorded moves and a household-label mismatch, following an unchanged starting address reaches the current coded book; a broken or cyclic route produces an explicit unresolved result instead of a presence assurance or handoff.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is a corrected once-daily location index. Both approaches handle corrected household labels, but after moves made without updating that index, it still names the original location; intact forwarding routes reach the latest location.
openings.defeat: Within the bounded exercise, a supposedly intact route ends at the wrong coded book, a broken route is accepted as resolved, or maintaining and checking the small sample already consumes ten clerk-minutes. Such results defeat the tested enabling capability or its preparation feasibility.
openings.probe: During preparation, the existing clerk assigns temporary opaque codes to six sample books and paper addresses within the existing shelves/cart. Keep reader details behind the desk. Move selected books twice, leaving forwarding cards; leave the starting index unchanged. Trace and record each lookup, then inject one missing pointer and one cycle. Verify destination codes, unresolved outcomes and total clerk time. Stop at ten minutes; make no reader handoffs in this exercise.
assumptions: Fit applies only to the capped probe. Full-scale preparation cost, queue effects and two-minute success remain unproven.
Every operational move would need a reliable forwarding update; an unrecorded move cannot be recovered by these pointers.
A trustworthy association between opaque hold codes and authorized readers is not established by the supplied evidence.
Long chains would require shortening or another bounded traversal rule before operational adoption.
